description: Committee recommends prohibiting other countries' flags at City Hall.
Requires Saskatoon-connected, registered non-profits for flag requests.
Councillor motion needed for third-party support requests to Council.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Administration cited geopolitical complexity for stopping foreign flag displays.
Charitable and non-profit organizations requesting flag raisings are affected.
Saskatoon would follow Regina's recent decision to stop flying foreign flags.
Flying foreign flags makes the city susceptible to criticism during conflicts.
Flying certain flags causes horrific memories for refugees from oppressive regimes.

description: Committee recommends 2026 Deputy Mayor schedule to Council.

Councillors can swap monthly duties if needed.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Councillors will serve monthly rotations as Deputy Mayor in 2026.

description: City infrastructure is valued at $23.3 billion.
Faces a $306.6 million funding gap over five years.
27% of assets have an unknown condition.

chips.text: Councillor Ford noted the infrastructure funding gap could be larger than reported.
The city will report on the state of infrastructure every two years.
The city aims to achieve zero percent unknown asset conditions.

description: Proposes 1% property tax increase for infrastructure.
Suggests using water utility reserves for asset management.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned if water utility payments to roads are truly ROI or a crosscharge.
Whether water utility payments to roads are ROI or a crosscharge remains unclear.
Administration will review water utility payments to roads for budget.

description: Reviews recreation facility usage bylaw due to anti-2SLGBTQIA+ rhetoric concerns.
Indigenous educators and youth faced hostility at a city event.
Council will consider new safeguards and a Two Spirit advisory table.

chips.text: Approved
Mayor Block clarified the motion reviews processes, not bans events, adhering to charter rights.
City Solicitor could not confirm if other city policies could be included in the review.
Jennifer Lenny called for stronger safeguards against hate in city facilities.
Councillor Ford highlighted potential legal risks and costs if events are cancelled.
Administration was already updating the recreation facilities usage file before the controversy.
